transcript.note: Round 1 — one complete batch, zero greens. Strategy: keep the ring's own winding and let the box be the ring's own extent instead of taking `suggest` (suggest rotates every station a quarter turn around the ring: it puts 32 at the top-LEFT while 32 currently sits top-RIGHT, so the whole assignment would have to travel ~1/4 of the perimeter). Instead I read the ring in its current order and assigned each station to the side it already lies nearest: top = 35, 32; right = 33, 39, 22, 29; bottom = 36, 0, 18, 25; left = 24, 47, 23. Box = the ring's own extremes, minX=6 (23/47), maxX=45 (22), and then rows chosen so the side is exactly 39 and no non-ring vertex lands ON an edge line: minY=2, maxY=41 (minY=3/4/5/6 would put 48(23,3)/52(27,4)/53(35,5)/8(20,6) exactly on the top edge = a swallowed point; row 2 and row 41 are empty). Corners: rather than spending greens I promoted the four stations that were already nearest each corner to BE the corner — 23→(6,2) TL, 32→(45,2) TR, 36→(45,41) BR, 24→(6,41) BL — so all 13 consecutive ring pairs are directly H/V and greens = 0. The one real hazard was the branch 32–20–21, which hangs OUTSIDE the ring to the right: with 32 left at (38,2) the segment 32→20(47,22) would have cut straight through the new right edge. Putting 32 on the corner (45,2) instead makes that segment leave the box tangentially (c>45 for every r>2), so the branch stays outside and 20/21 need not move at all. 25 goes to the bottom edge (12,41) rather than the left edge, because on the left edge its segment to 12(16,49) would have crossed the bottom edge at c=8. Everything is submitted as one batch (targets for all 13 ring stations, 22 included as a no-op freeze) so only the final state is judged; pre-checked offline: 0 swallowed points, 0 crossings (base 0), all 58 vertices' 360-degree edge orders unchanged.
